scenes.description: Chalkboard opening: 'Newton's Laws of Motion' header. A sliding block on a rough plane decelerates as an opposing red vector arrow labeled 'Friction' flashes into view.
scenes.overlay_notes: Title card at top, animated friction vector diagram in center
scenes.shot_intent: Hook viewer curiosity by challenging their intuitive assumption that motion requires continuous push
scenes.information_role: Introduce the hidden enemy of motion: friction

scenes.description: First Law (Inertia): Deep slate cosmos canvas with stars. A golden Voyager-style space probe glides smoothly across the screen. Floating formula: 'Net Force = 0 -> Velocity = Constant'.
scenes.overlay_notes: Law 1 Header with floating mathematical vector equation
scenes.shot_intent: Visually demonstrate that without friction, motion continues indefinitely
scenes.information_role: Define Newton's First Law and Inertia

scenes.description: Second Law (F = ma): Interactive chalk balance diagram. On left: Soccer ball (0.4 kg) hit with 50N force launches with large velocity vector. On right: Boulder (400 kg) hit with same 50N barely nudges. Formula highlights: 'a = F / m'.
scenes.overlay_notes: Split comparison illustrating mass resistance to acceleration
scenes.shot_intent: Give tangible intuition for F=ma as mass resisting acceleration
scenes.information_role: Teach calculation and ratio of Force, Mass, and Acceleration

scenes.description: Third Law (Action-Reaction): Rocket propulsion diagram on chalkboard. Exhaust gas fires downward (Orange arrow: Force on gas). Rocket accelerates upward (Cyan arrow: Force on rocket). Highlighting text box: 'Forces act on DIFFERENT bodies!'.
scenes.overlay_notes: Opposing vector arrows with colored caller tags
scenes.shot_intent: Dismantle the myth that action-reaction forces cancel out

scenes.description: The Golden Rule Card: Bold dark chalkboard card with radiant chalk border. Big typography: 'Forces do NOT cause motion. Unbalanced forces cause CHANGE in motion.' Checkmarks next to key concepts.
scenes.overlay_notes: High contrast typography card with particle chalk dust
scenes.shot_intent: Deliver the core takeaway rule for exam mastery
scenes.information_role: Reinforce the single most critical physics takeaway

scenes.description: Outro & Practical Connection: Passenger in a braking car showing inertia vector towards seatbelt. Final chalkboard slate: 'Thank Inertia! Follow for More Physics Made Simple'.
scenes.overlay_notes: Animated subscribe icon and seatbelt safety callout
scenes.shot_intent: Connect theory to real-world experience and invite channel follow
